[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Per the operators own site (q.com/data-centers/richmond-1/, reached via a redirect from qtsdatacenters.com), this Sandston, Virginia campus, named Richmond 1 (matching this registrys RIC1 naming), spans a 207 acre site, totals 2.3 million square feet of current space, and provides 238 MW of campus power capacity, described by the operator as the largest and most connected data center campus in the area. DC1 through DC3 share the address 6000 Technology Blvd, Sandston, VA 23150; the page also lists DC4 (3560 Portugee Rd), DC5 (3540 Portugee Rd) and DC6 (3520 Portugee Rd), which are not present as separate rows in this registry under the RIC1 name. This is a campus aggregate figure across multiple buildings, not a single building total, so it is recorded as a capacity_note rather than critical_it_mw. The operator name on these rows (Quality Technology Services) is the pre-2013-IPO name of the same company now formally called QTS Realty Trust, Inc. (per the English Wikipedia article on QTS Realty Trust); QTS Realty Trust has been added as an alias on this operator row (uid 8a29e4ff) rather than renaming this row, consistent with the never rename or delete policy. A separate Richmond 2 campus (this registrys RIC2 rows) is a distinct, newer, still partly under-construction QTS campus a short distance away, per a companion Richmond 2 operator page.

profile.regional_context: QTS was founded in 2003 by Chad Williams, went public via IPO in 2013, and was acquired by Blackstone (via Blackstone Infrastructure Partners and BREIT) for approximately $10 billion, completed August 31, 2021, at $78/share. QTS is headquartered in Overland Park, Kansas.
profile.facility_type_note: Part of QTS's Richmond, Virginia mega-campus, spanning Henrico County and Sandston. This is QTS's flagship facility story: in 2010 QTS converted a former semiconductor manufacturing site into what Wikipedia describes as a 1.3 million square foot mega data center.

reading.body:
The Richmond 1 campus spans 207 acres and 2.3 million square feet across multiple buildings in Henrico County and Sandston, Virginia. The operator publishes 238 MW of aggregate power capacity for the entire campus. At 10 kW per rack, a conservative estimate for mixed colocation workloads, this represents roughly 23,800 racks; at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, the same capacity could support roughly 5,950 racks. The operator describes this as the largest and most connected data center campus in the regional area.

Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities, but only 23 publish power capacity figures. This campus ranks 24th by published megawatts in the state, with 238 MW against a state total of 1,375 MW, representing 17 percent of Virginia's disclosed capacity. The published capacity figures for Virginia are sparse enough that this ranking reflects data availability as much as absolute scale.

The campus converted from a former semiconductor manufacturing site beginning in 2010 and remains in active operation as part of QTS Realty Trust's portfolio. Whether this facility matters to AI scaling depends on whether its power capacity aligns with AI workload demand, which is not published here. The operator's published specifications do not disclose current utilization, tenant composition, cooling infrastructure, or power procurement terms.
